key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization.
engineering_relevance: These slow local polarization dynamics could inform halide-perovskite device models, although photovoltaic performance was not evaluated.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials.
Analysis of local polar ordering and relaxation across perovskite materials.
Investigation of chain-by-chain polarization reversal in ferroelectric CsGeBr3.
evidence_signal: Simulations reveal polar chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales—four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 intermediate.
watch_item: Experimental confirmation and links to solar-cell efficiency or stability are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
